newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's SCI to spend $1.3 bln for oil tankers.
newsitem.headline: India's SCI to spend $1.3 bln for oil tankers.

text.p: The Shipping Corporation Of India Ltd (SCI) is planning to spend up to US$1.3 billion over the next six years to renew its fleet of oil tankers, chairman and managing director P.K. Srivastava told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday.
"We will be spending nearly between US$1,200 and $1,300 million...to buy new and old tankers," Srivastava said on the sidelines of a World Tanker Outlook conference in Singapore.
He said SCI would raise the funds "by a combination of international resources, commercial borrowing and raising equity in the capital market".
SCI is 80-percent owned by the Indian government and 20-percent of its shares are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
Over the next few years, the government plans to divest its shareholding down to 49 percent, Srivastava said.
About 30 tankers in SCI's fleet of 50 tankers will be replaced by either newly built or younger tankers, he said.
SCI's fleet currently has a capacity of well over three million deadweight tons.
Srivastava said the company would not be replacing its very large crude carrier (at least 160,000 dwt) when it is scrapped because only one port in India can handle it.
"Our priority is to replace the Suezmax (between 60,000-100,000 dwt) and Aframax (between 100,000-200,00 dwt) tankers which can enter into our Indian ports," he said.
SCI ships nearly 70 percent of India's total crude oil requirements and about 30 percent of its oil products and chemical needs, he said.
